Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

Six air job / OWL forms were filed on 11/15. Only one carries a stop-work selection at all, and it is the routine item. These are reported so the technicians can confirm what they meant, not as confirmed events.

"Stop work authority was discussed" — Brianda Sandoval, XTO Energy, BROOK B-17B 8H, job 37015. This is the pre-job discussion item, not "Stop work authority utilized", which was not selected. Her narrative reads "the crew had to blow down" and "crew finished the well in a timely manner". Nothing on the form describes an unsafe condition. This reads as a normal pre-job entry.

Neither stop-work item selected — 1099 Robert Henigan on BROOK B-17B 8H (37016) and BROOK A-5D 4H (37014); Jordan Lemmons on MIDKIFF UNIT 102H (37029_1); 1099 Joseph Popillion on MIDKIFF UNIT 102H (37029_2).
"Unsafe conditions" was not selected on any form on 11/15.

One form is not the mis-selection pattern and should be looked at on its own: Brianda Sandoval, XTO Energy, BROOK A-5D 4H, job 37013, 08:19 AM to 12:31 PM. Her entire OWL section was submitted with nothing selected — no observation items, no "what went well" items, no close-out. The only narrative on the form sits in the wrong field, under "How did we leave this location better than we found it?", and reads "job got canceled. too much pressure on the outer casing". That is a named well condition that stopped the job, recorded with no corresponding selection anywhere on the form. This is the inverse of the usual problem and it is the one item on the day worth confirming with the technician. Her paired form on the other well that afternoon (37015) was filled out in full, so this is not a pattern across her day.

1099 Robert Henigan's form for the same cancelled job (37014) selected "Job scope completed safely and as planned" on a job his own form records as cancelled after two minutes on site, with "Canceled" entered into four narrative fields. The selection and the narrative contradict each other and need his confirmation.
None of these technicians appeared on the stop-work confirmation list in the 09/26 or 11/11 reviews.

Justin Pack — H2S daily on Hughes #1, complete cascade and hydro entries, all photos same-day, FR Yes. 1099 Marcos Morales — H2S daily on St Elmo, all photos captured inside a nine-minute window, FR Yes. Alexander Clubb — field service 37032, details completed. 1099 Robert Henigan — air job 37016 on BROOK B-17B 8H, OWL completed
No gas or H2S reading above zero was recorded on any form on 11/15. No incident and no near miss was reported. Jordan Lemmons's form on MIDKIFF UNIT 102H explicitly records all zeros.

Trailer Inspection Forms, Trailer Readiness Forms and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based, so a defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images and not as text, so they cannot be checked here. Where a photo is dated well before the form, as in the five cases listed above, the condition it records may also be out of date.

32 of 32 submissions read. The job board was available: the 11/15/2026 Ark-La-Tex & Permian Basin boards arrived from Blake Walton at 10:36 AM Central and the 11-15 sheet of each was used. 25 live manned board rows were checked for coverage — 17 on the Permian sheet and 8 on the Ark-La-Tex sheet, after excluding rows marked ON STANDBY, DAYS OFF, MOBILIZING and WTX SUPPORT. This run started at 11:06 PM Central, before the Central day closed, so any form submitted after that time is not in these counts; the two missing Trailer Readiness Forms are the finding most often resolved by a late submission, and no search of the following morning was possible because 11/16 had barely begun.
